blocks.text: Rokku (ロック; Rock) is a sub-style of Gyaru that incorporates elements of goth, punk, and visual kei. It is darker in fashion than other gyaru styles, with a heavy emphasis on black clothing, intense eye makeup, and Gothic imagery like skulls and crosses. Unlike many substyles, Rokku does not require a tan, and instead places focus on personal creativity through makeup, hair and accessorizing.

Although the exact origins of Rokku are not known, it got popular around the mid to late 2000s, with popular gal magazines such as EGG featuring the style, and clothing brands like GLAVIL by tutuHA, Ghost of Harlem, Gilfy, and GLAD NEWS. Many gals who wore Rokku were also Bangya, a term meant to refer to female fans of Visual Kei. Because of that, the subculture and even style of Rokku was related and inspired by Vkei.

The color palette for Rokku is much darker than a typical gyaru aesthetic. Black is the basis of most Rokku looks, with red, gray, silver, and sometimes pink filling out the rest of the palette. Cheetah print is common in this aesthetic, as is plaid, skeletal bones and skulls, stripes, crosses, and spikes. Most Gothic imagery fits within this trend and can be used to strengthen a Rokku look. Hair can be bleached or dyed any color, and typically skin is kept pale instead of tanned.
Skin: Bright and pale, luminous skin rather than the traditional deep tan accented in other gyaru substyles.
Materials: Heavy use of faux leather, studs, fishnets, and chains.
Details: Safety pins, stripes, ripped fabrics, distressed hems and plaid patterns.
Lenses: Bright or unnatural-colored contact lenses (also known as circle lenses) to make eyes appear larger.
Lips: Light pink, pale, or occasionally moody and dark lip colors.
Contour: Light and sharp nose contouring or bleached eyebrows.
Body modification: Visible tattoos and body piercings are very common in this Rokku substyle.
Styling: Layered, spikey visual kei-inspired cuts, teased, voluminous curls, or heavy side-swept bangs with fringes.
